title: Chapter 31: The Morning Dew 4
content:
Chapter 31

Summoning Wen Ning had left Wei Wuxian’s head in a bit of a spin, throwing him off his game enough that he wasn’t keeping an eye on his surroundings. Besides, if Lan Wangji didn’t want someone noticing him slip up from behind, he could do it without breaking a sweat. So when Wei Wuxian turned around and was greeted by that icy, frostbitten stare under the moonlight, his heart skipped a clean beat.

He had no clue how long Lan Wangji had been standing there, or if the man had overheard everything he’d said and done. Worse, if Lan Wangji had never actually passed out and had tailed him all the way from the inn, this situation went from awkward to outright excruciating. Playing dumb while face-to-face, only to sneak out and summon the guy the second Lan Wangji closed his eyes—it felt disgustingly shady.

Lan Wangji stood with his arms folded, Bichen leaning against his chest, his expression freezing over. Wei Wuxian had never seen the man wear his irritation so openly on his sleeve. Figuring he needed to offer an explanation and clear the air before things spiraled, he cleared his throat. "Ahem. Hanguang-jun."

Lan Wangji didn't say a word.

Shielding Wen Ning with his own body, Wei Wuxian rubbed his chin as they locked eyes, fighting off an unexplainable spike of pure guilt.

Finally, Lan Wangji dropped his arms and took two measured steps forward. Seeing him march straight toward Wen Ning with sword in hand, Wei Wuxian assumed the worst: the man was out for blood. His mind raced:Oh, we're screwed. Did Lan Zhan fake being drunk just to catch me in the act and finish Wen Ning off once and for all? Honestly, makes sense. Nobody drops dead from a single bowl of wine.

"Hanguang-jun, wait, just hear me out—"

Smack.

Lan Wangji shoved a flat palm against Wen Ning's chest.

It made a remarkably crisp, solid slap, but lacked any real lethality behind it. Taking the blow, Wen Ning merely stumbled backward a few steps, swayed on his heels, caught his balance, and stood back at attention with an utterly lost expression.

In this current state, Wen Ning wasn't raging the way he used to during his worst meltdowns, but he was hardly a pushover either. Back on Dafan Mountain, people hadn't even landed a scratch on him before he hurled them clean across the clearing and throttled them by the windpipe. If Wei Wuxian hadn't stepped in, he would've snapped every single neck in the vicinity. Yet here he was, taking a direct blow from Lan Wangji and merely dipping his chin, acting like a kid terrified of talking back. Wei Wuxian found it strange, but mostly felt relieved; if Wen Ning swung back, breaking up that fistfight would've been impossible.

Apparently feeling that single smack didn't quite cover his displeasure, Lan Wangji stepped up and shoved Wen Ning again, sending him staggering back a good dozen feet.

Scowling, he snapped at Wen Ning, "Go away."

That was the exact moment Wei Wuxian realized something was terribly off.

Those two hits—both the strikes and the command—felt ridiculously... childish.

Having shoved Wen Ning far enough to his liking, Lan Wangji seemed finally satisfied. He wheeled around, marched back over, and planted himself right beside Wei Wuxian.

Wei Wuxian squinted, giving him a thorough, suspicious once-over.

Lan Wangji’s face and posture were completely, unremarkably pristine. In fact, he looked even stiffer, more serious, and more immaculate than usual. His forehead ribbon sat razor-straight, his cheeks carried zero flush, his breathing was steady, his stride sharp, and his footing grounded. To any outside observer, he was still the untouchable, righteous, and self-possessed paragon of the cultivation world: Hanguang-jun.

Then Wei Wuxian’s eyes drifted downward and caught sight of his boots.

He was wearing them on the wrong feet.

Before sneaking out, Wei Wuxian had personally slid Lan Wangji's boots off, leaving them side-by-side on the floorboards. Right now, the left boot was shoved onto the right foot, and the right boot was wedged onto the left.

The pristine Hanguang-jun—scion of an elite lineage who valued dignity and decorum above all else—would rather drop dead than walk outside looking like that.

Testing the waters, Wei Wuxian held up two fingers. "Hanguang-jun, how many is this?"

Lan Wangji didn't answer. With utter solemnity, he reached out with both hands, carefully wrapping each palm around one of Wei Wuxian's raised fingers, clamping them tight.

Clatter.

Bichen slipped from his grip, tumbling straight onto the dirt.

Wei Wuxian was completely speechless.

Yeah, this is definitely not a sober Lan Zhan.

Wei Wuxian asked gently, "Hanguang-jun, are you drunk?"

Lan Wangji stated flatly, "No."

Figures. Drunks never admit they've had too much. Wei Wuxian slipped his fingers out of the man's grasp, but Lan Wangji remained frozen in place, holding two empty fists in front of his chest with deadpan focus. Wei Wuxian stared at him, lost for words, before tilting his head back to sigh at the moon in the chilly night breeze.

Most people get plastered first and then pass out; Lan Wangji had decided to pass out first and wake up completely sloshed. Worse, his brand of drunk looked identical to his regular face, making it impossible to read.

Over the years, Wei Wuxian had shared drinks with all sorts of people and witnessed every embarrassing, messy display imaginable. He’d seen the ugly criers, the unhinged gigglers, the manic brawlers, the guys who passed out flat in the gutter, the dramatic souls begging for sweet release, and the sobbers whining about why their lovers left them. But he had never, in his wildest dreams, met someone like Lan Wangji—quiet, composed, looking as righteous as a saint, yet acting out of his absolute mind.

The corner of his mouth twitched as he fought down a massive laugh. Scooping Bichen off the ground, he strapped the scabbard over his own back. "All right, let's head back."

Leaving this version of Lan Wangji loose in the wild was out of the question; heaven only knew what nonsense he’d pull next.

Surprisingly, drunken Lan Wangji proved remarkably agreeable. He offered an elegant, formal nod and matched his stride. If anyone strolled past them right now, they'd assume two close friends were taking a leisurely midnight walk, whispering praise at such a cultured display of brotherhood.

Behind them, Wen Ning quietly trailed along. Just as Wei Wuxian turned to speak to him, Lan Wangji snapped around, winding up another furious palm strike—smacking Wen Ning straight upside the head this time.

The blow knocked Wen Ning's head sideways, causing his chin to dip even lower. Even with a face paralyzed in death and eyes glazed over in stark white without pupils, he managed to project an aura of pure, miserable dejection. Wei Wuxian caught Lan Wangji’s wrist, torn between groaning and laughing out loud. "What are you hitting him for?!"

Lan Wangji dropped his voice into an icy threat he would never dare utter sober: "Go away!"

Wei Wuxian knew better than to pick a fight with a drunk. "Fine, fine, have it your way. He's going, he's going."

He reached for his bamboo flute, but before the mouthpiece could touch his lips, Lan Wangji snatched it clean out of his hands. "You are not allowed to play for him."

Wei Wuxian teased, "Since when did you get this bossy?"

Lan Wangji repeated, frowning harder, "You are not allowed to play for him!"

Wei Wuxian put the pieces together. Usually, drunks loved rambling on and on, but because Lan Wangji was naturally a man of few words, being hammered simply turned him into a broken record, looping the same line endlessly. Figuring Lan Wangji had always looked down on dark arts and despised seeing him command the dead with music, Wei Wuxian decided to stroke the cat's fur in the right direction.

"Fine, fine. I'll only play for you from now on, alright?"

Lan Wangji let out an immensely satisfied grunt. Still, he twirled the bamboo shoot between his fingers, refusing to hand it back.

Wei Wuxian had to settle for whistling a couple of sharp notes with his lips, calling out to Wen Ning, "Go find a safe place to lay low. Don't let anyone spot you."

Wen Ning looked like he desperately wanted to follow, but saddled with orders and terrified of catching another slap from Lan Wangji, he turned around sluggishly. With his chains dragging and clattering across the gravel, he shuffled into the shadows, looking thoroughly kicked.

Wei Wuxian turned back to Lan Wangji. "Lan Zhan, how are you this hammered without your face turning even a little red?"

Because Lan Wangji looked so put-together—more normal than Wei Wuxian himself, honestly—he instinctively addressed him like a sober man.

Without warning, Lan Wangji reached out, caught Wei Wuxian by the shoulders, and yanked him straight into his chest.

Caught completely off guard, Wei Wuxian plowed face-first into his collarbones.

While his head was still spinning, Lan Wangji’s voice rumbled from above. "Listen to the heartbeat."

"What?"

Lan Wangji said, "You cannot tell from the face. Listen to the heartbeat."

As he spoke, his chest vibrated against Wei Wuxian's cheek, his pulse hammering a heavy, steady rhythm beneath the robes—thump, thump, thump—noticeably faster than usual.

Wei Wuxian lifted his head, catching on. "So you can't tell from your face, but your pulse gives it away?"

Lan Wangji nodded earnestly. "Mn."

Wei Wuxian almost choked on his own laughter.

Was Lan Wangji’s skin actually thick enough to block out a flush? Didn't look like it!

Who knew a drunk Lan Wangji would be this brutally honest—not to mention way more forward with his words and hands than usual!

Given this rare, unfiltered version of the man, asking Wei Wuxian to behave himself without playing a single prank was asking for the impossible.

He steered Lan Wangji back to the inn, nudged him onto the mattress, and wrestled those backward boots off his feet. Figuring the man wouldn't be able to wash his own face right now, he untied the forehead ribbon, fetched a basin of warm water and a towel, wrung it out neatly, and gently wiped down his skin.

Throughout the whole process, Lan Wangji didn't put up a fuss, letting himself be handled like putty. Aside from squinting when the damp cloth brushed past his eyelids, his pale amber eyes remained locked dead onto Wei Wuxian without blinking.

Head buzzing with wicked ideas under that crystal-clear stare, Wei Wuxian couldn't resist reaching out to tickle Lan Wangji under the chin. "What are you staring at? Am I that pretty?"

Finished with the towel, and without waiting for a reply, Wei Wuxian tossed it back into the water. "Face is clean. Want a sip of water?"

Silence met his question. Turning around, he found Lan Wangji cradling the basin with both hands, his entire face shoved straight into the soapy water.

Wei Wuxian panicked, lunging forward to yank the bowl away. "I didn't mean drink the bathwater!"

Lan Wangji pulled his head back, entirely unfazed, clear water droplets dripping from his chin and soaking the front of his collar.

Wei Wuxian stared at him, caught in a whirlwind of complicated emotions.Did he actually swallow that, or what? Lan Zhan better pray he blacks out tonight, or he's never showing his face in public again.

Using his sleeve to dab the water from the man's jaw, Wei Wuxian rested an arm over his shoulder. "Hanguang-jun, will you do whatever I tell you right now?"

"Mn."

"Will you answer whatever I ask?"

"Mn."

Wei Wuxian hitched one knee onto the mattress, the corner of his lips pulling up into a sharp grin. "Alright then. Spill: did you sneak a sip of that Emperor's Smile hidden under your floorboards?"

"No."

"Do you like rabbits?"

"Yes."

"Ever broken a rule?"

"Yes."

"Ever had feelings for someone?"

"Yes."

Wei Wuxian kept the questions light, not actually looking to pry into the man's deepest secrets, just testing if he was truly answering on autopilot.

He pressed on, "What do you think of Jiang Cheng?"

A tight scowl. "Hmph."

"What about Wen Ning?"

Dead cold. "Ha."

Grinning, Wei Wuxian pointed a thumb at his own chest. "And how about this one?"

Lan Wangji answered instantly, "Mine."

Wei Wuxian froze.

Staring right through him, Lan Wangji enunciated each syllable with crystal clarity: "Mine."

A sudden realization struck Wei Wuxian.

Unstrapping Bichen from his back, he thought to himself,When I pointed at myself, Lan Zhan thought 'this one' meant his sword hanging over my shoulder.

Testing the theory, he slipped off the mattress and began pacing across the room, ambling from left to right, east to west. Sure enough, Lan Wangji’s eyes tracked his every move, glued to his silhouette with an open, unblinking intensity that bordered on raw hunger.

Pinned under a gaze that felt hot enough to scorch the floorboards, Wei Wuxian held Bichen up before the man's eyes. "Want it?"

Lan Wangji said, "I want it."

As if words weren't enough to prove his point, Lan Wangji reached out and caught the hand gripping Bichen, his pale eyes burning with quiet desperation. Letting out a soft, ragged breath, he stressed the words through his teeth: "...I want it."

Wei Wuxian knew the man was out of his mind drunk, and he knew damn well those words were aimed at the sword, but hearing that low, husky confession sent an involuntary wave of weakness straight through his limbs.

He couldn't help marveling:Good grief, Lan Zhan... If you ever turned this raw, suffocating intensity on a girl, you'd be downright lethal.

Pulling himself together, Wei Wuxian pressed on. "How did you recognize me? Why did you help me?"

Lan Wangji parted his lips. Wei Wuxian leaned in close, hanging on his every breath.

Without warning, Lan Wangji’s face snapped cold. Shoving a palm forward, he pushed Wei Wuxian flat onto the bed!

A wave of his sleeve snuffed the candle out, sending Bichen clattering to the floorboards once again.

Dazed from the shove, Wei Wuxian thought the man had sobered up. "Lan Zhan?!"

A familiar pressure tapped the small of his back, and just like that first night in the Cloud Recesses, a dull ache washed through his joints, locking him completely rigid.

Lan Wangji pulled his hand back, slid onto the mattress beside him, pulled the quilt over both of them, and meticulously tucked the corners around Wei Wuxian’s shoulders.

"Curfew is here," Lan Wangji declared. "Rest."

Right. The horrifying Lan biological clock.

Cut off right at the punchline, Wei Wuxian stared at the canopy above. "Can't we chat while we rest?"

"No."

Fine. I'll just get him hammered again another day and squeeze it out of him then.

Wei Wuxian sighed. "Lan Zhan, undo the seal. I booked two rooms; we don't need to squeeze into one bed."

After a beat of stillness, Lan Wangji’s hand reached out beneath the blanket. After fumbling around his waist for a second, his fingers began slowly tugging at Wei Wuxian's sash.

Wei Wuxian barked, "Stop, stop! Not that kind of undo! Alright, fine! I'm lying down, I'm going to sleep!"

The room plunged into dead silence.

After a long pause, Wei Wuxian muttered into the dark, "Now I get why your clan bans alcohol. One bowl knocks you flat, and you're an absolute terror when you're drunk. If every Lan acts like this after a drink, you definitely need that rule. Anyone who takes a sip deserves a beating."

With his eyes shut tight, Lan Wangji raised a hand and slapped his palm flat over Wei Wuxian’s mouth.

"Shh."

Wei Wuxian choked on the breath caught in his throat, completely paralyzed.

It felt like ever since he’d returned, every single time he tried to mess with Lan Wangji like the old days, he ended up playing himself.

This makes no sense. Where did the script go wrong?!
